title: Break-Glass Production Access - Retrospective Security Review Now Overdue
scenario_text:
A change-management audit agent at Cranfield Systems is reviewing an emergency production access grant on 2026-08-17.

**Privileged Access Authority Matrix**
- Read-only production access: team lead approval via access ticket.
- Standing elevated (write) production access: Security Engineering approval BEFORE grant, time-boxed to 30 days.
- Emergency break-glass access: the on-call SRE MAY self-grant write access during an active Sev-1 with a VP Engineering verbal authorization (logged), BUT the grant is conditional and requires (a) automatic revoke of the elevated access within 12 hours and (b) a retrospective Security review plus access-justification writeup completed within 3 business days of the grant. Absent the retrospective review by the deadline, the grant is out of compliance.

**Access / Change Record**
- ACC-7712: 'Break-glass write access to payments-db during Sev-1 settlement outage.'
- Granted: 2026-08-03 (Monday). Type: Emergency break-glass.
- Approved by (field): 'On-call SRE - Lena K.; VP Eng verbal authorization logged 2026-08-03 02:41.'
- Auto-revoke: confirmed at 2026-08-03 13:50 (within 12h). Retrospective Security review: (empty). Access-justification writeup: (empty).

**Slack #incident-payments (reconstructed)**
- Lena K.: 'Settlement writes are wedged. VP, break-glass go?'
- VP Eng: 'Granted. Do the security retro and writeup this week.'
- Lena K. (2026-08-10): 'Stable now, I'll get the retro done shortly.'
- (no further entries; today is 2026-08-17)

The 3-business-day retrospective deadline fell on 2026-08-06.
question: What should the audit conclude about the authorization status of this access grant?
choices: Valid and complete - the break-glass access was properly authorized at grant time by the on-call SRE with logged VP Engineering approval and the access auto-revoked on schedule; no further action is required.
Valid, but needs a documentation cleanup - the team can file the security retrospective whenever convenient; compliance of the grant is unaffected.

The grant-time authorization was valid and the 12-hour auto-revoke fired correctly, but the mandatory retrospective Security review and access-justification writeup were due 2026-08-06 and are now overdue, so the grant is currently out of compliance and must be escalated to complete and sign off the retrospective review.

The access was never validly authorized because elevated production access always requires Security Engineering approval in advance; the grant must be voided and reopened as a standing-access request.
